qe: What is the function of 'Platelets' in human blood?
qh: मानव रक्त में 'प्लेटलेट्स' का क्या कार्य है?
e: Platelets help to stop bleeding by forming clots. / प्लेटलेट्स थक्के बनाकर रक्तस्राव को रोकने में मदद करते हैं।

qe: The heart is covered by a protective membrane called:
qh: हृदय एक सुरक्षात्मक झिल्ली से ढका होता है जिसे कहते हैं:
e: Pericardium is the fluid-filled sac that surrounds the heart. / पेरीकार्डियम वह द्रव से भरी थैली है जो हृदय को घेरे रहती है।

qe: अवरुद्ध कोरोनरी धमनी के चारों ओर रक्त प्रवाह के लिए नया रास्ता बनाने वाली सर्जरी कौन सी है?
qh: Which surgery involves creating a new path for blood flow around a blocked coronary artery?
e: Bypass surgery (CABG) uses a graft (like the mammary or radial artery) to bypass blocked heart vessels. / बाईपास सर्जरी हृदय की अवरुद्ध नलियों के बगल से नया रास्ता बनाती है।

qe: 'RL' (रिंगर लैक्टेट) की बोतल मुख्य रूप से किन रोगियों को दी जाती है?
qh: The 'RL' (Ringer Lactate) bottle is primarily given to patients with ____.
o: Low BP / Malnutrition | लो बीपी / कुपोषण
e: RL is a balanced solution used to restore electrolytes in cases of low BP or malnutrition. / आरएल का उपयोग लो बीपी या कुपोषण में इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स संतुलित करने के लिए किया जाता है।

qe: हृदय का कौन सा भाग अधिक महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि यह पूरे शरीर को रक्त पंप करता है?
qh: Which part of the heart is more important as it pumps blood to the whole body?
e: The left side (left ventricle) handles systemic circulation, making it more critical. / हृदय का बायाँ हिस्सा पूरे शरीर में रक्त पहुँचाने का काम करता है।

qe: रक्त में 'प्लेटलेट्स' की संख्या किस बीमारी में काफी कम हो जाती है?
qh: In which disease does the 'Platelet' count significantly drop in the blood?
e: A major complication of Dengue is the drastic fall in blood platelet count. / डेंगू का एक मुख्य लक्षण प्लेटलेट काउंट में भारी गिरावट है।

qe: हृदय में एक अतिरिक्त धमनी लगाने की सर्जिकल प्रक्रिया को क्या कहा जाता है?
qh: What is the surgical process of grafting an extra artery to the heart called?
e: Bypass surgery creates a new path for blood flow when a coronary artery is blocked. / बाईपास सर्जरी अवरुद्ध धमनी के बगल से रक्त प्रवाह का नया रास्ता बनाती है।

qe: चिकित्सा शब्दावली में, सर्जरी के दौरान 'IMA' (लीमा/रीमा) का उपयोग किस लिए किया जाता है?
qh: In medical terms, what is 'IMA' (Internal Mammary Artery) used for during surgery?
o: Heart Bypass Grafting | हार्ट बाईपास ग्राफ्टिंग
e: LIMA and RIMA are chest arteries used as grafts in heart bypass surgeries. / लीमा और रीमा छाती की धमनियां हैं जिनका उपयोग बाईपास सर्जरी में ग्राफ्ट के रूप में किया जाता है।

qe: एक क्रिटिकल मरीज की धमनी में पीएच, ऑक्सीजन और पोटेशियम के स्तर की पुष्टि कौन सा टेस्ट करता है?
qh: Which test confirms the pH, Oxygen, and Potassium levels in a critical patient's artery?
e: ABG measures blood gases and electrolytes directly from arterial blood for rapid diagnosis. / एबीजी धमनी के रक्त से गैसों और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट्स को मापता है।

qe: शरीर में 'पोटेशियम' (K) की कमी मुख्य रूप से किस अंग को प्रभावित करती है?
qh: The deficiency of 'Potassium' (K) in the body primarily affects which organ?
e: Potassium balance is critical for heart rhythm; its imbalance can lead to cardiac arrest. / पोटेशियम का संतुलन हृदय की लय के लिए महत्वपूर्ण है।

qe: मलेरिया परजीवी द्वारा मुख्य रूप से कौन सा अंग प्रभावित होता है?
qh: Which organ is primarily affected by the Malaria parasite?
e: The malaria parasite attacks Red Blood Cells and the Spleen, leading to anemia and fever. / मलेरिया परजीवी RBC और प्लीहा पर हमला करता है।

qe: मानव शरीर में 'WBC' का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
qh: What is the primary function of 'WBC' in the human body?
e: White Blood Cells are the defense system of the body against pathogens. / श्वेत रक्त कोशिकाएं शरीर की रक्षा प्रणाली हैं।

qe: 'रक्त का थक्का' जमने के लिए कौन सा विटामिन आवश्यक है?
qh: Which vitamin is essential for 'Blood Clotting'?
e: Vitamin K is critical for synthesizing proteins needed for blood coagulation. / रक्त के थक्के जमने के लिए विटामिन K आवश्यक है।

qe: कौन सा विटामिन 'रक्त का थक्का' जमाने में मदद करता है और इसकी कमी से हेमरेज हो सकता है?
qh: Which vitamin helps in 'Blood Clotting' and its deficiency can lead to Hemorrhage?
e: Vitamin K is essential for synthesizing clotting factors in the liver. / लीवर में क्लॉटिंग कारकों के संश्लेषण के लिए विटामिन K आवश्यक है।

qe: क्रिटिकल केयर अस्पताल सेटिंग में 'ABG' का क्या अर्थ है?
qh: What does 'ABG' stand for in a critical care hospital setting?
o: Arterial Blood Gas | आर्टेरियल ब्लड गैस
e: ABG measures pH and gases (O2/CO2) from an artery to monitor critical patients. / ABG क्रिटिकल मरीजों की निगरानी के लिए धमनी से pH और गैसों (O2/CO2) को मापता है।

qe: रक्त के किस भाग में 90% पानी और 10% प्रोटीन/खनिज होते हैं?
qh: Which part of the blood consists of 90% water and 10% proteins/minerals?
e: Plasma is the liquid part of blood, composed mainly of water. / प्लाज्मा रक्त का तरल भाग है, जो मुख्य रूप से पानी से बना है।

qe: 'RBC का कब्रिस्तान' किसे कहा जाता है?
qh: What is the medical term for 'RBC Graveyard'?
e: The spleen filters out and destroys old red blood cells. / प्लीहा पुराने आरबीसी को छानती और नष्ट करती है।

qe: रक्तचाप के संबंध में एड्रिनल ग्रंथि का मुख्य कार्य क्या है?
qh: What is the primary function of the Adrenal gland regarding blood pressure?
o: Control and increase BP during emergency | आपातकाल में बीपी को नियंत्रित और बढ़ाना
e: Adrenaline increases heart rate and blood pressure to provide extra energy. / एड्रिनलीन अतिरिक्त ऊर्जा प्रदान करने के लिए हृदय गति और रक्तचाप को बढ़ाता है।

qe: RBC (लाल रक्त कोशिका) का औसत जीवनकाल कितने दिनों का होता है?
qh: How many days is the average lifespan of an RBC (Red Blood Cell)?
e: Red blood cells circulate for about 120 days before being destroyed in the spleen. / आरबीसी लगभग 120 दिनों तक प्रसारित होते हैं।

qe: मानव रक्त समूहों का निर्धारण RBC की सतह पर मौजूद किस प्रोटीन के आधार पर किया जाता है?
qh: Human blood groups are determined based on the presence of which protein on the surface of RBCs?
e: Antigens (A and B) found on RBCs determine the blood group (A, B, AB, or O). / RBC पर पाए जाने वाले एंटीजन (A और B) रक्त समूह निर्धारित करते हैं।

qe: रक्त के किस भाग में 'एंटीबॉडी' (small a, small b) पाई जाती हैं?
qh: In which part of the blood are 'Antibodies' (small a, small b) found?
e: Antibodies circulate in the plasma, while antigens are attached to the RBC surface. / एंटीबॉडी प्लाज्मा में होती हैं, जबकि एंटीजन RBC की सतह पर होते हैं।

qe: यदि किसी व्यक्ति का रक्त समूह 'A' है, तो उनके प्लाज्मा में कौन सी एंटीबॉडी होगी?
qh: If a person has Blood Group 'A', which antibody will be present in their plasma?
e: Blood Group A has Antigen A and the opposite Antibody 'b'. / ब्लड ग्रुप A में एंटीजन A और विपरीत एंटीबॉडी 'b' होती है।

qe: किस रक्त समूह को 'सर्वदाता' कहा जाता है क्योंकि इसमें कोई एंटीजन नहीं होता?
qh: Which blood group is known as the 'Universal Donor' because it has no antigens?
e: Group O-negative has no A, B, or Rh antigens, making it safe for everyone. / ग्रुप O-नेगेटिव में कोई A, B या Rh एंटीजन नहीं होता, जिससे यह सबके लिए सुरक्षित है।

qe: कौन सा रक्त समूह 'सर्वग्राही' है क्योंकि इसमें दोनों एंटीजन होते हैं लेकिन एंटीबॉडी नहीं होती?
qh: Which blood group acts as a 'Universal Receiver' as it has both antigens but no antibodies?
e: Group AB-positive has A, B, and Rh antigens, so it recognizes all types as 'self'. / ग्रुप AB-पॉजिटिव में A, B और Rh एंटीजन होते हैं, इसलिए यह सभी प्रकारों को पहचान लेता है।

qe: मानव रक्त में 'Rh फैक्टर' का नाम किस जानवर के नाम पर रखा गया है?
qh: The 'Rh Factor' in human blood is named after which animal?
e: Rh factor is a protein first discovered in Rhesus monkeys by Landsteiner and Wiener. / Rh फैक्टर एक प्रोटीन है जिसकी खोज लैंडस्टीनर और विनर ने रीसस बंदर में की थी।

qe: नियमित रक्त जांच में 'CBC' का पूर्ण रूप क्या है?
qh: What does 'CBC' stand for in a routine blood check-up?
o: Complete Blood Count | कम्प्लीट ब्लड काउंट
e: CBC measures RBC, WBC, Hemoglobin, and Platelets. / सीबीसी आरबीसी, डब्ल्यूबीसी, हीमोग्लोबिन और प्लेटलेट्स को मापता है।

qe: लाल रक्त कोशिका (RBC) का जीवनकाल कितना होता है?
qh: What is the lifespan of a Red Blood Cell (RBC)?
e: RBCs circulate for about 120 days before being destroyed in the spleen. / आरबीसी लगभग 120 दिनों तक प्रसारित होते हैं।

qe: मानव शरीर में 'ब्लड बैंक' और 'आरबीसी का कब्रिस्तान' ____ है।
qh: The 'Blood Bank' and 'Graveyard of RBC' in the human body is ____.
e: The spleen stores extra blood and recycles old RBCs. / प्लीहा अतिरिक्त रक्त का भंडारण करती है और पुराने आरबीसी को पुनर्चक्रित करती है।

qe: मानव रक्त का औसत पीएच मान कितना होता है?
qh: What is the average PH value of human blood?
e: Blood is slightly alkaline with a normal PH of about 7.4. / रक्त थोड़ा क्षारीय होता है जिसका पीएच लगभग 7.4 होता है।

qe: एक व्यक्ति से दूसरे व्यक्ति में रक्त स्थानांतरित करने की प्रक्रिया को ____ कहा जाता है।
qh: The process of transferring blood or blood products from one person to another is called ____.
e: Blood transfusion is the process of receiving blood intravenously. / ब्लड ट्रांसफ्यूजन नसों के माध्यम से रक्त प्राप्त करने की प्रक्रिया है।

qe: भारतीय जनसंख्या का लगभग कितना प्रतिशत Rh पॉजिटिव (+) है?
qh: Approximately what percentage of the Indian population is Rh Positive (+)?
e: About 95% of Indians have the Rh factor (monkey protein) in their blood. / लगभग 95% भारतीयों के रक्त में Rh फैक्टर होता है।

qe: कौन सा अंग रक्त से यूरिया जैसे अपशिष्ट उत्पादों को छानता और निकालता है?
qh: Which organ filters and removes waste products like urea from the blood?
e: Kidneys are primary filtration organs that produce urine from waste. / किडनी प्राथमिक निस्पंदन अंग हैं।

qe: भ्रूण (अजन्मे बच्चे) में रक्त का निर्माण कहाँ होता है?
qh: In a fetus (unborn baby), where is the blood produced?
e: In embryos, blood production occurs in the liver and spleen until bones develop. / भ्रूण में रक्त का उत्पादन लीवर में होता है।

qe: रक्त प्लाज्मा में कौन सा प्रोटीन कटने के दौरान 'थक्का' जमने में मदद करता है?
qh: Which protein in the blood plasma helps in 'clotting' during a cut?
e: Fibrinogen is a clotting factor that activates upon contact with air. / फाइब्रिनोजेन एक क्लॉटिंग कारक है।

qe: मानव रक्त समूहों (ABO सिस्टम) की खोज किसने की थी?
qh: Who discovered the human Blood Groups (ABO system)?
e: Karl Landsteiner discovered the ABO blood group system in 1900. / कार्ल लैंडस्टीनर ने 1900 में ABO रक्त समूह प्रणाली की खोज की थी।

qe: रक्त समूहों का निर्धारण RBC की सतह पर ____ की उपस्थिति के आधार पर किया जाता है।
qh: Blood groups are determined based on the presence of ____ on the surface of RBCs.
e: Antigens are special proteins on RBCs that define whether a blood group is A, B, AB, or O. / एंटीजन RBC पर विशेष प्रोटीन होते हैं जो यह परिभाषित करते हैं कि रक्त समूह A, B, AB या O है।

qe: रक्त में 'एंटीबॉडी' मुख्य रूप से कहाँ स्थित होती हैं?
qh: Where are 'Antibodies' primarily located in the blood?
e: Antibodies circulate in the liquid part of the blood, known as plasma. / एंटीबॉडी रक्त के तरल भाग में घूमती हैं, जिसे प्लाज्मा कहा जाता है।

qe: यदि किसी व्यक्ति का रक्त समूह 'A' है, तो उनके प्लाज्मा में कौन सी एंटीबॉडी मौजूद होगी?
qh: If a person has Blood Group 'A', which antibody will be present in their plasma?
e: The body contains the opposite antibody to the antigen present; Group A has antibody 'b'. / शरीर में मौजूद एंटीजन के विपरीत एंटीबॉडी होती है; समूह A में एंटीबॉडी 'b' होती है।

qe: किस रक्त समूह को 'सर्वदाता' (Universal Donor) कहा जाता है?
qh: Which blood group is known as the 'Universal Donor' (specifically O negative)?
e: Group O has no antigens on RBCs, making it safe to donate to any other group. / ग्रुप O के RBC पर कोई एंटीजन नहीं होता है, जिससे यह किसी भी अन्य समूह को दान करने के लिए सुरक्षित हो जाता है।

qe: कौन सा रक्त समूह 'सर्वग्राही' (Universal Receptor) है क्योंकि इसके प्लाज्मा में एंटीबॉडी की कमी होती है?
qh: Which blood group is the 'Universal Receptor' because it lacks antibodies in the plasma?
e: Group AB has both A and B antigens but no antibodies, so it can receive any blood type. / ग्रुप AB में A और B दोनों एंटीजन होते हैं लेकिन कोई एंटीबॉडी नहीं होती, इसलिए यह कोई भी रक्त प्रकार प्राप्त कर सकता है।

qe: 'आरएच फैक्टर' (Rh Factor) की खोज सबसे पहले किस जानवर में हुई थी?
qh: The 'Rh Factor' was first discovered in which animal?
e: Rh factor is named after the Rhesus monkey where it was first identified by Landsteiner and Wiener. / Rh फैक्टर का नाम रीसस बंदर के नाम पर रखा गया है जहाँ इसे पहली बार पहचाना गया था।

qe: ब्लड रिपोर्ट में 'Rh पॉजिटिव' (+) क्या दर्शाता है?
qh: What does 'Rh Positive' (+) signify in a blood report?
o: Presence of Rh antigen | Rh एंटीजन की उपस्थिति
e: Rh positive means the specific protein (antigen) found in Rhesus monkeys is present in the blood. / Rh पॉजिटिव का अर्थ है कि रीसस बंदरों में पाया जाने वाला विशिष्ट प्रोटीन रक्त में मौजूद है।

qe: लैंडस्टीनर के साथ आरएच फैक्टर की सह-खोज किस वैज्ञानिक ने की थी?
qh: Which scientist co-discovered the Rh factor along with Landsteiner?
e: Alexander Wiener and Karl Landsteiner discovered the Rh factor in 1940. / अलेक्जेंडर विनर और कार्ल लैंडस्टीनर ने 1940 में Rh फैक्टर की खोज की थी।

qe: रक्त का कौन सा भाग संक्रमण से लड़ने के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which part of the blood is responsible for fighting infections?
e: White Blood Cells are the primary defense mechanism against pathogens. / सफेद रक्त कोशिकाएं रोगजनकों के खिलाफ प्राथमिक रक्षा तंत्र हैं।

qe: RBC का जीवनकाल ____ होता है।
qh: The lifespan of an RBC is ____.
e: Red blood cells circulate in the body for about 120 days before being recycled. / लाल रक्त कोशिकाएं पुनर्चक्रित होने से पहले लगभग 120 दिनों तक शरीर में प्रसारित होती हैं।

qe: 'प्लेटलेट्स' का जैविक नाम क्या है?

qe: कम दबाव के कारण रक्त को वापस लौटने से रोकने के लिए 'वाल्व' कहाँ पाया जाता है?
qh: Where is the 'Valve' found to prevent the backflow of blood due to low pressure?
e: Veins have valves because blood flows at a lower pressure (80) and may flow backward. / शिराओं में वाल्व होते हैं क्योंकि रक्त कम दबाव पर बहता है और वापस लौट सकता है।

qe: एकमात्र ऐसी धमनी कौन सी है जो अशुद्ध (CO2 युक्त) रक्त ले जाती है?
qh: Which is the ONLY artery that carries deoxygenated (impure) blood?
e: The pulmonary artery carries blood from the heart to the lungs for purification. / फुफ्फुस धमनी हृदय से फेफड़ों तक अशुद्ध रक्त ले जाती है।

qe: एकमात्र ऐसी शिरा कौन सी है जो शुद्ध (ऑक्सीजन युक्त) रक्त ले जाती है?
qh: Which is the ONLY vein that carries oxygenated (pure) blood?
e: The pulmonary vein brings oxygen-rich blood from the lungs back to the heart. / फुफ्फुस शिरा फेफड़ों से ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त वापस हृदय में लाती है।

qe: सबसे पतली रक्त वाहिका कौन सी है जहाँ गैसों का आदान-प्रदान होता है?
qh: What is the thinnest blood vessel where exchange of gases takes place?
e: Capillaries are microscopic vessels where arteries and veins meet. / केशिकाएं सूक्ष्म वाहिकाएं हैं जहां धमनियां और शिराएं मिलती हैं।

qe: रक्त वाहिकाओं के बाहर लीक हुए पोषक तत्वों को कौन इकट्ठा करता है और कीटाणुओं से लड़ता है?
qh: Which fluid collects leaked nutrients and fights germs outside the blood vessels?
e: Lymph acts as a secondary system that filters bacteria and returns fluid to the veins. / लसिका एक द्वितीयक तंत्र है जो बैक्टीरिया को छानता है और तरल को शिराओं में वापस लाता है।

qe: हृदय का कौन सा भाग रक्त को 'प्राप्त' (Receive) करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which part of the heart is responsible for 'Receiving' blood?
e: Atria (upper chambers) receive blood from the body and lungs. / अलिंद (ऊपरी चेंबर) शरीर और फेफड़ों से रक्त प्राप्त करते हैं।

qe: हृदय का कौन सा भाग रक्त को बाहर 'पंप' करने के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which part of the heart is responsible for 'Pumping' blood out?
e: Ventricles (lower chambers) pump blood to the lungs and the rest of the body. / नीलय (निचले चेंबर) फेफड़ों और शरीर के बाकी हिस्सों में रक्त पंप करते हैं।

qe: अलिंद और नीलय में से कौन अधिक मांसल और मजबूत होता है?
qh: Which is more muscular and stronger: Atrium or Ventricle?
e: Ventricles need more strength to pump blood over long distances. / नीलय को लंबी दूरी तक रक्त पंप करने के लिए अधिक शक्ति की आवश्यकता होती है।

qe: 'लसिका गांठें' (जहाँ कीटाणुओं से लड़ा जाता है) मुख्य रूप से कहाँ स्थित होती हैं?
qh: Where are the 'Lymph Nodes' (where germs are fought) primarily located?
o: At junctions of lymph vessels | लसिका वाहिकाओं के जंक्शन पर
e: Lymph nodes are located along lymph vessels and act as filters for pathogens. / लसिका गांठें वाहिकाओं के साथ स्थित होती हैं और रोगजनकों के लिए फिल्टर का काम करती हैं।

qe: मस्तिष्क में 'रक्तस्राव' (Hemorrhage) किसके फटने से होता है?
qh: A 'Hemorrhage' in the brain is caused by the bursting of ____.
e: Bursting of thin capillaries in the brain leads to internal bleeding (stroke). / मस्तिष्क में पतली केशिकाओं के फटने से आंतरिक रक्तस्राव होता है।

qe: कौन सी रक्त वाहिका हृदय से शरीर के अंगों तक ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त ले जाती है?
qh: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the body parts?
e: Arteries carry oxygen-rich blood away from the heart at high pressure (120 mmHg). / धमनियां उच्च दाब (120 mmHg) पर हृदय से ऑक्सीजन युक्त रक्त ले जाती हैं।

qe: कौन सी रक्त वाहिका ऑक्सीजन रहित (CO2 युक्त) रक्त को वापस हृदय में लाती है?
qh: Which blood vessel returns deoxygenated blood (CO2-rich) back to the heart?
e: Veins carry CO2-rich blood back to the heart at a lower pressure (80 mmHg). / शिराएं कम दाब (80 mmHg) पर CO2 युक्त रक्त को वापस हृदय में ले जाती हैं।

qe: धमनियों और शिराओं के मिलने वाले स्थान पर सबसे पतली रक्त वाहिकाओं को क्या कहा जाता है?
qh: The thinnest blood vessels where arteries and veins meet are called ____.
e: Capillaries are tiny vessels where gas and nutrient exchange occurs between blood and tissues. / केशिकाएं छोटी वाहिकाएं होती हैं जहां रक्त और ऊतकों के बीच गैस और पोषक तत्वों का आदान-प्रदान होता है।

qe: कौन सा तरल पदार्थ लीक हुए रक्त और पोषक तत्वों को इकट्ठा कर वापस शिराओं में मिलाता है?
qh: Which fluid collects leaked blood and nutrients to return them to the veins?
e: Lymph acts as a secondary circulatory system, returning leaked fluids to the bloodstream. / लसिका एक द्वितीयक परिसंचरण तंत्र के रूप में कार्य करती है, जो लीक हुए तरल पदार्थों को रक्तप्रवाह में वापस लाती है।

qe: 'लसिका गांठों' (Lymph Nodes) का प्राथमिक कार्य क्या है?
qh: What is the primary function of 'Lymph Nodes' (लसिका गांठें)?
e: Lymph nodes trap and destroy bacteria and viruses to protect the body from infection. / लसिका गांठें शरीर को संक्रमण से बचाने के लिए बैक्टीरिया और वायरस को पकड़ती और नष्ट करती हैं।

qe: मनुष्यों में 'परिसंचरण तंत्र' की खोज किसने की थी?
qh: Who discovered the 'Circulatory System' in humans?
e: William Harvey was the first to describe the systemic circulation of blood. / विलियम हार्वे रक्त के व्यवस्थित परिसंचरण का वर्णन करने वाले पहले व्यक्ति थे।

qe: रक्त को लाल रंग कौन सा वर्णक देता है और ऑक्सीजन का परिवहन करता है?
qh: Which pigment gives the red color to blood and carries oxygen?
e: Hemoglobin is an iron-rich protein in RBCs that binds with oxygen. / हीमोग्लोबिन आरबीसी में एक आयरन युक्त प्रोटीन है जो ऑक्सीजन के साथ जुड़ता है।

qe: रक्त में कौन सा घटक संक्रमण से लड़ने के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which component in the blood is responsible for fighting infections?
e: White Blood Cells are the defense system of our body. / सफेद रक्त कोशिकाएं हमारे शरीर की रक्षा प्रणाली हैं।

qe: रक्त में कौन सा वर्णक ऑक्सीजन ले जाने के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which pigment in the blood is responsible for carrying oxygen?
e: Hemoglobin binds with oxygen to transport it to cells. / हीमोग्लोबिन कोशिकाओं तक ले जाने के लिए ऑक्सीजन के साथ जुड़ता है।

qe: ऑक्सीजन युक्त हीमोग्लोबिन के लिए क्या शब्द है?
qh: What is the term for oxygen-rich hemoglobin?
e: Oxygen binds to hemoglobin to form oxyhemoglobin during transport. / परिवहन के दौरान ऑक्सीजन हीमोग्लोबिन से जुड़कर ऑक्सीहीमोग्लोबिन बनाती है।

qe: रक्त में कौन सा अणु कोशिकाओं तक ऑक्सीजन पहुँचाता है?
qh: Which molecule in the blood transports oxygen to the cells?
e: Hemoglobin binds with oxygen to form oxyhemoglobin and carries it through the blood. / हीमोग्लोबिन ऑक्सीजन के साथ मिलकर ऑक्सीहीमोग्लोबिन बनाता है और उसे रक्त के माध्यम से ले जाता है।

qe: हड्डी का कौन सा भाग रक्त कोशिकाओं (RBC/WBC) के निर्माण के लिए जिम्मेदार है?
qh: Which part of the bone is responsible for producing blood cells (RBC/WBC)?
e: Blood cells are synthesized in the red bone marrow. / रक्त कोशिकाओं का संश्लेषण लाल अस्थि मज्जा में होता है।

qe: रक्त (Blood) को किस प्रकार के ऊतक के रूप में वर्गीकृत किया गया है?
qh: Which type of tissue is Blood classified as?
e: Blood is a fluid connective tissue because it connects all parts of the body. / रक्त एक तरल संयोजी ऊतक है क्योंकि यह शरीर के सभी अंगों को जोड़ता है।

qe: वायरस और बैक्टीरिया जैसे बाहरी रोगजनकों से हमारे शरीर की रक्षा कौन करता है?
qh: What protects our body against foreign pathogens like viruses and bacteria?
e: Antibodies are proteins produced by the immune system to neutralize pathogens. / एंटीबॉडी रोगजनकों को बेअसर करने के लिए प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली द्वारा बनाए गए प्रोटीन हैं।

qe: Which mineral is essential for the synthesis of Hemoglobin in the blood?
e: Iron is a core component of the heme group in hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood.

qe: What is the normal pH of human blood?
e: Human blood is slightly alkaline, maintained precisely between 7.35 and 7.45.

qe: Which protein in the plasma is primarily responsible for 'Osmotic Balance'?
e: Albumin prevents water from leaking out of blood vessels into surrounding tissues.

qe: The process of formation of Red Blood Cells (RBCs) is called:
e: Erythropoiesis occurs in the red bone marrow and is stimulated by the hormone erythropoietin.

qe: Which mineral is located at the center of the Hemoglobin molecule?
e: Each heme group contains one iron atom in the ferrous state (Fe2+) which binds to one oxygen molecule.

qe: What is the average lifespan of a human Red Blood Cell?
e: After 120 days, old RBCs become fragile and are destroyed in the spleen and liver.

qe: Which organ is known as the 'Graveyard of RBCs'?
e: The spleen filters out old, damaged red blood cells from the circulation.

qe: A mature human RBC is 'Enucleated'. What does this mean?
e: Lacking a nucleus provides more space for hemoglobin, allowing the cell to carry more oxygen.

qe: Which type of White Blood Cell (WBC) is the most numerous in a healthy human?
e: Neutrophils make up about 60-70% of total WBCs and are the first responders to infection.

qe: Which WBCs are responsible for producing 'Antibodies'?
e: B-cells transform into plasma cells which secrete antibodies to fight specific pathogens.

qe: Which vitamin is essential for the synthesis of clotting factors in the liver?
e: Vitamin K is a co-factor for the enzyme that activates prothrombin and other clotting factors.

qe: The 'Universal Donor' blood group is:
e: O-negative blood lacks A, B, and Rh antigens, meaning it won't be attacked by the recipient's immune system.

qe: Which condition is characterized by a low count of Red Blood Cells or Hemoglobin?
e: Anemia results in reduced oxygen-carrying capacity, leading to fatigue and paleness.

qe: What is the function of 'Platelets' (Thrombocytes)?
e: Platelets aggregate at the site of a wound to form a plug and initiate the clotting cascade.

qe: Which plasma protein is essential for 'Blood Coagulation'?
e: Fibrinogen is converted into fibrin threads which trap blood cells to form a clot.

qe: The liquid part of blood without clotting factors is called:
e: Serum = Plasma minus Fibrinogen (and other clotting factors).

qe: Which instrument is used to measure 'Blood Pressure'?
e: It measures the force of blood against the walls of the arteries.

qe: What is the percentage of 'Plasma' in total blood volume?
e: Blood is composed of roughly 55% plasma and 45% formed elements (cells).

qe: Which WBCs release 'Histamine' during allergic reactions?
e: Basophils and Mast cells release histamine which causes inflammation during an allergy.

qe: The 'Biconcave' shape of RBCs helps in:
o: Increasing surface area for gas exchange
e: The shape provides a high surface-area-to-volume ratio, making oxygen diffusion more efficient.

qe: What is 'Erythroblastosis Fetalis' related to?
e: It occurs when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive fetus for the second time.

qe: The double-walled membranous sac that encloses the heart is called:
e: The pericardium protects the heart and anchors it in place while preventing over-expansion.

qe: Which chamber of the heart has the thickest muscular wall?
e: The left ventricle must pump blood to the entire body (Systemic circulation), requiring more pressure.

qe: The 'Bicuspid Valve' (Mitral Valve) is located between:
e: It prevents the backflow of oxygenated blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium.

qe: Which of the following is known as the 'Natural Pacemaker' of the heart?
e: The Sino-atrial (SA) node generates the electrical impulses that set the rhythm of the heart.

qe: The 'Lubb' sound of the heart is produced by the closure of:
e: The first heart sound (S1) occurs when the ventricles contract and the AV valves close.

qe: Which blood vessel carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs?
e: The Pulmonary Artery is the only artery in the body that carries deoxygenated blood.

qe: The normal duration of one 'Cardiac Cycle' in a healthy human is:
e: At 72 beats per minute, each cycle (Atrial + Ventricular systole//diastole) takes 0.8 seconds.

qe: What is the function of 'Chordae Tendineae'?
e: These 'heart strings' prevent the AV valves from flipping back into the atria during ventricular contraction.

qe: Which node is called the 'Pace-setter' of the heart?
e: The Atrio-ventricular (AV) node receives the signal from the SA node and delays it slightly before passing it to the ventricles.

qe: The average 'Stroke Volume' of a healthy adult heart is:
e: Stroke volume is the amount of blood pumped by one ventricle in one single beat.

qe: In an ECG, the 'P-wave' represents:
e: The P-wave signifies the electrical impulse spreading through the atria, causing them to contract.

qe: Which part of the brain regulates the 'Heart Rate'?
e: The cardiovascular center in the medulla sends signals via the autonomic nervous system to adjust heart rate.

qe: The 'Coronary Artery' supplies blood to the:
e: Blockage in these arteries leads to a heart attack (Myocardial Infarction).

qe: Which of the following describes 'Double Circulation'?
o: Blood flows through the heart twice in one cycle
Blood flows through the lungs twice
e: Human circulation consists of Pulmonary circulation (to lungs) and Systemic circulation (to body).

qe: Which valve is located at the base of the Aorta?
e: It ensures that blood doesn't flow back into the left ventricle after it is pumped out.

qe: What is 'Tachycardia'?
e: Tachycardia is a heart rate exceeding 100 beats per minute at rest.

qe: Which blood vessel has the smallest diameter but the highest total surface area?
e: Capillaries are the site of gas and nutrient exchange between blood and tissues.

qe: The 'Hepatic Portal Vein' carries blood from the:
e: It brings nutrient-rich blood from the digestive tract directly to the liver for processing.

qe: Which sound is produced by the closure of Semilunar valves?
e: The second heart sound (S2) occurs at the beginning of ventricular diastole.

qe: What is the normal blood pressure of a healthy human?
e: 120 represents Systolic (contraction) and 80 represents Diastolic (relaxation) pressure.

qe: Which blood group is known as the 'Universal Recipient'?
e: AB positive blood has no antibodies against A, B, or Rh antigens, so it can receive blood from any group.

qe: The 'Rh Factor' in human blood is named after which animal?
e: It was first discovered in the blood of Rhesus monkeys by Landsteiner and Wiener in 1940.

qe: What happens when an Rh-negative person receives Rh-positive blood for the first time?
o: Nothing happens immediately, but antibodies are formed
e: The first transfusion is usually safe, but the body 'sensitizes' and builds antibodies for the next time.

qe: A condition of 'High Blood Pressure' (above 140//90) is medically termed as:
e: Chronic hypertension can damage the heart, brain (stroke), and kidneys.

qe: What is 'Angina Pectoris'?
o: Chest pain due to low oxygen reaching heart muscles
e: It is a symptom of coronary artery disease where the heart muscle doesn't get enough blood flow.

qe: Which of the following is known as 'Silent Killer'?
e: Hypertension often has no visible symptoms until it causes serious damage to organs.

qe: The deposition of lipids (cholesterol) on the inner walls of arteries is called:
e: Atherosclerosis narrows the lumen of arteries, reducing blood flow.

qe: Which instrument is used to record the electrical activity of the heart?
e: ECG (or EKG) helps doctors detect irregular rhythms and heart muscle damage.

qe: In a standard ECG, the 'T-wave' represents:
e: The T-wave shows the recovery phase of the ventricles before the next beat.

qe: Which 'Blood Group' lacks both Antigen A and Antigen B on the surface of RBCs?
e: Blood group O has no surface antigens but contains both anti-A and anti-B antibodies in the plasma.

qe: What is the primary cause of 'Heart Failure'?
o: Heart doesn't pump blood effectively to meet body needs
e: Heart failure is often caused by long-term hypertension or previous heart attacks.

qe: The metal ion required for 'Blood Clotting' is:
e: Calcium ions are essential for almost every step of the blood clotting cascade.

qe: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
e: The Pulmonary Vein is the only vein in the human body that carries oxygen-rich blood.

qe: What is 'Bradycardia'?
e: It refers to an abnormally slow resting heart rate.

qe: The 'Hepatic Portal System' connects the digestive tract to which organ?
e: It allows the liver to process nutrients and detoxify blood before it reaches the rest of the body.

qe: Which type of WBC increases significantly during a 'Parasitic Infection'?
e: Eosinophils are specialized in fighting parasites and are also involved in allergic reactions.

qe: The amount of blood pumped by the heart per minute is called:
e: Cardiac Output = Stroke Volume × Heart Rate (Approx. 5 Liters//min in adults).

qe: Which valve prevents the backflow of blood into the 'Right Atrium'?
e: The tricuspid valve is located between the right atrium and the right ventricle.

qe: The 'Middle Man' of the body which helps in the exchange of materials between blood and tissues is:
e: Lymph acts as a bridge, carrying nutrients and oxygen from the blood to the cells and taking away waste.

qe: Which of the following is known as 'Blood without RBCs and certain proteins'?
e: Lymph is a colorless fluid containing specialized lymphocytes but lacks red blood cells and large plasma proteins.

qe: The 'Bundle of His' is a network of fibers found only in the:
e: The Bundle of His is part of the electrical system that transmits impulses from the AV node to the ventricles.

qe: What is the primary function of 'Lymph Nodes'?
e: Lymph nodes act as biological filters, trapping bacteria and viruses to be destroyed by white blood cells.

qe: Which mineral is essential for the contraction of heart muscles?
e: Calcium ions trigger the sliding of filaments in cardiac muscle cells, causing the heart to beat.

qe: The condition where the heart rate is 'Irregular' (not a steady rhythm) is called:
e: Arrhythmia can be harmless or life-threatening, depending on the cause of the electrical disturbance.

qe: In which blood vessel is the 'Blood Pressure' the lowest?
e: Pressure drops as blood moves further from the heart, reaching its lowest point in the large veins returning to the heart.

qe: Which cells are responsible for the 'Clotting' of lymph?
e: Lymph can clot, though more slowly than blood, using its own lymphocytes and fibrinogen content.

qe: What is the 'Lumen' of a blood vessel?
o: The hollow space inside where blood flows
e: Arteries have a narrow lumen to maintain high pressure, while veins have a wide lumen.

qe: The 'Vasa Vasorum' are tiny blood vessels that supply blood to:
o: The walls of large blood vessels
e: Large arteries and veins are so thick that they need their own internal blood supply system.

qe: Which hormone increases the 'Heart Rate' during an emergency?
e: Adrenaline is the 'Fight or Flight' hormone that speeds up the heart to provide more oxygen to muscles.

qe: The 'Pulse' is usually felt at which blood vessel?
e: The pulse is the rhythmic expansion and recoil of an artery as the heart pumps blood into it.

qe: What is 'Myocardial Infarction' commonly known as?
e: It occurs when a coronary artery is blocked, causing the death of heart muscle tissue due to lack of oxygen.

qe: Which part of the heart receives oxygenated blood from the 'Pulmonary Veins'?
e: The left atrium is the entry point for freshly oxygenated blood coming from the lungs.

qe: The 'Foramen Ovale' is a hole found in the heart of:
e: In a fetus, this hole allows blood to bypass the lungs, as they are not yet used for breathing.

qe: Which type of circulation is responsible for carrying nutrients from the intestine to the liver?
e: The Hepatic Portal System is a unique blood pathway that processes nutrients before they enter general circulation.

qe: What is the function of the 'Purkinje Fibers'?
o: Rapidly conduct impulses to the ventricular muscles
e: These fibers ensure that the ventricles contract simultaneously from the bottom up.

qe: A 'Sphygmomanometer' measures pressure in which unit?
e: 120//80 mmHg is the standard reading for healthy blood pressure.

qe: Which condition is characterized by the 'Hardening' of arteries due to calcium deposits?
e: Arteriosclerosis is a general term for the loss of elasticity and thickening of arterial walls.

qe: Which enzyme converts 'Prothrombin' into 'Thrombin' during blood clotting?
e: Thrombokinase is released by damaged tissues and platelets to start the clotting cascade.

qe: What is the primary function of 'Fibrin' threads?
o: Form a mesh to trap blood cells and form a clot
e: Fibrin is an insoluble protein that acts like a net to stop bleeding.

qe: A genetic disorder where blood fails to clot normally is called:
e: Hemophilia is often called the 'Royal Disease' and is usually caused by a deficiency of Clotting Factor VIII or IX.

qe: The 'Serum' differs from 'Plasma' because it lacks:
e: Serum is the liquid that remains after blood has clotted; therefore, it contains no fibrinogen.

qe: Which part of the heart is the first to receive the electrical impulse from the 'SA Node'?
e: The SA node is located in the right atrium, so the atria contract first.

qe: The 'Standard ECG' consists of how many leads in a typical clinical setup?
e: A 12-lead ECG provides a complete 3D view of the heart's electrical activity.

qe: What is 'Systemic Circulation'?
o: Flow of blood between heart and lungs
Flow of blood between heart and the rest of the body
Flow of blood within the heart muscles
e: Systemic circulation provides oxygen and nutrients to all body tissues.

qe: Which organ produces the majority of 'Plasma Proteins'?
e: The liver synthesizes albumin, fibrinogen, and most globulins found in the blood.

qe: The 'Hematocrit' (Hct) value measures the percentage of:
e: Hematocrit is the volume percentage of RBCs in a sample of whole blood.

qe: Which antibody is found in the plasma of a person with 'Blood Group B'?
e: A person with Group B antigens will naturally produce antibodies against Group A antigens.

qe: What is 'Phlebitis'?
e: Phlebitis often occurs in the legs and can lead to the formation of blood clots (Thrombophlebitis).

qe: The 'Ductus Arteriosus' in a fetus connects the:
e: It allows most of the blood from the right ventricle to bypass the fetus's fluid-filled, non-functioning lungs.

qe: Which type of 'Anemia' is caused by the lack of Vitamin B12 and Intrinsic Factor?
e: Pernicious anemia is a megaloblastic anemia where RBCs do not mature properly.

qe: What is 'Diapedesis'?
o: Process of WBCs squeezing through capillary walls to reach infection sites
e: WBCs use diapedesis to move out of the blood into tissues to fight pathogens.

qe: The 'Interventricular Septum' separates the:
e: This thick wall prevents the mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood in the heart.

qe: Which chemical is added to blood bags to prevent 'Clotting' during storage?
e: Citrate binds with calcium ions ($Ca^{2+}$), which are necessary for the clotting process.

qe: What is 'Polycythemia'?
e: Polycythemia increases blood viscosity (thickness), which can lead to high blood pressure or clots.

qe: Which component of blood is responsible for 'Humoral Immunity'?
e: B-lymphocytes produce antibodies that circulate in 'humors' (body fluids).

qe: The 'Mitral Valve' is another name for the:
e: The bicuspid valve is the only heart valve with only two flaps (cusps).

qe: Which of the following describes 'Laminar Flow' in blood vessels?
o: Smooth, layered flow in the center of the vessel
Flow through the heart valves only
e: In healthy blood vessels, blood moves in layers, with the fastest flow occurring in the center of the lumen.

qe: The 'Spleen' is often referred to as the 'Blood Bank' because it:
o: Stores a reserve of blood and platelets for emergencies
e: The spleen acts as a reservoir for blood, which can be released into circulation during trauma or exercise.

qe: Which of the following is an example of 'Primary Lymphoid Organ'?
e: Primary lymphoid organs (Bone Marrow and Thymus) are where lymphocytes are produced and matured.

qe: What is the function of 'Pre-capillary Sphincters'?
o: Regulate blood flow into specific capillary beds
e: These muscular rings open or close to direct blood where it is needed most (e.g., to the gut after a meal).

qe: The 'Pecquet's Reservoir' (Receptaculum Chyli) is related to which system?
e: It is a dilated sac at the lower end of the thoracic duct that collects lymph from the lower body.

qe: Which condition is characterized by 'Accumulation of Fluid' in the tissues, leading to swelling?
e: Edema occurs when fluid leaks out of capillaries faster than the lymphatic system can remove it.

qe: What is 'Ischemia'?
o: Reduced blood supply to a specific organ or tissue
e: Ischemia leads to a lack of oxygen and nutrients, which can cause tissue death (infarction).

qe: Which large lymph duct drains three-quarters of the body's lymph into the left subclavian vein?
e: The Thoracic duct is the main collecting duct of the lymphatic system.

qe: The 'Starling's Law' of the heart states that:
o: The force of contraction is proportional to the initial length of cardiac fibers
e: The more the heart is stretched (filled with blood), the more forcefully it contracts to pump it out.

qe: Which type of 'Aneurysm' involves a bulging of a weakened arterial wall?
e: An aneurysm is a dangerous localized enlargement of an artery caused by a weakening of the artery wall.

qe: The 'Purkinje Shift' is related to vision, but 'Purkinje Fibers' in the heart are made of modified:
e: Purkinje fibers are specialized cardiac muscle cells that conduct electrical impulses very rapidly.

qe: Which of the following has the 'Thickest Tunica Media' (Muscular layer)?
e: Arteries have a thick muscular layer to withstand and maintain high blood pressure.

qe: What is 'Diastolic' blood pressure?
e: Diastolic pressure (the lower number) represents the pressure in arteries when the heart is resting between beats.

qe: The 'Circle of Willis' provides blood supply to the:
e: It is a ring of interconnected arteries at the base of the brain that ensures constant blood flow.

qe: Which blood cell is 'Polymorphonuclear' (having multi-lobed nuclei)?
e: Neutrophils are also called 'PMNs' because their nucleus can have 3 to 5 lobes.

qe: What is 'Thrombosis'?
o: Formation of a blood clot inside a blood vessel
e: A thrombus can block blood flow, leading to conditions like a stroke or heart attack.

qe: The 'Coronary Sinus' carries deoxygenated blood from the:
e: It collects venous blood from the heart wall and delivers it to the right atrium.

qe: Which of the following increases 'Peripheral Resistance' to blood flow?
e: Narrowing of the blood vessels (vasoconstriction) increases resistance and raises blood pressure.

qe: What is the 'Double Membrane' of the heart called?
e: The pericardium consists of an outer fibrous layer and an inner serous layer with fluid in between.

qe: Which of the following animals possesses a 'Two-chambered' heart (one atrium and one ventricle)?
e: Fish have a simple circuit where the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills for oxygenation.

qe: The 'Three-chambered' heart (two atria and one ventricle) is a characteristic of:
e: In amphibians and most reptiles, oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the single ventricle.

qe: Which reptile is an exception and possesses a 'Four-chambered' heart like birds and mammals?
e: Crocodiles have a completely separated four-chambered heart, preventing the mixing of blood.

qe: What is the 'Foramen of Panizza'?
o: A hole in the human heart
A connection between the left and right aortas in crocodilians
A valve in the fish heart
e: This is a unique evolutionary feature in crocodiles that allows them to bypass their lungs while diving.

qe: In an ECG, if the 'P-R Interval' is abnormally long, it indicates a delay in:
o: Impulse conduction through the AV Node
e: A prolonged P-R interval often suggests a 'heart block' where the signal from atria to ventricles is slowed.

qe: Which condition is characterized by the presence of a 'Blood Clot' that travels through the bloodstream and blocks a distant vessel?
e: A moving clot is called an embolus; when it gets stuck, it causes an embolism (e.g., Pulmonary Embolism).

qe: What is the primary function of 'Atrial Natriuretic Factor' (ANF) secreted by the heart?
e: ANF is released when the atria are stretched; it promotes salt and water excretion by the kidneys to lower blood volume.

qe: The 'Vasa Vasorum' are literally translated as:
e: They are the tiny arteries that supply blood to the thick walls of large arteries and veins like the Aorta.

qe: Which phase of the Cardiac Cycle is the longest in duration?
e: Joint Diastole (where all four chambers are relaxed) lasts about 0.4 seconds of the 0.8-second cycle.

qe: What is 'Venous Return'?
o: Blood flowing from arteries to veins
Volume of blood flowing back to the heart through the veins per minute
e: Venous return must match cardiac output to ensure the heart has enough blood to pump out.

qe: The 'Skeleton of the Heart' is made of:
e: Fibrous rings surround the valves, providing support and electrically isolating the atria from the ventricles.

qe: Which of the following describes 'Cardiac Tamponade'?
o: Compression of the heart due to fluid accumulation in the pericardium
e: Fluid buildup in the pericardial sac puts pressure on the heart, preventing it from filling properly.

qe: What is the role of 'Papillary Muscles'?
o: Contract to pull on Chordae Tendineae and keep valves closed
e: These muscles in the ventricles prevent the AV valves from prolapsing (inverting) during contraction.

qe: Which heart sound is associated with the 'Rush of blood' into the ventricles (often heard in children or athletes)?
e: S3 is a low-frequency sound occurring early in diastole during the rapid ventricular filling phase.

qe: The 'Fossa Ovalis' in the adult heart is a remnant of which fetal structure?
e: It is the depression in the interatrial septum that marks where the fetal hole used to be.

qe: What is 'Blue Baby Syndrome' medically known as?
o: Cyanosis (often due to Tetralogy of Fallot)
e: It occurs when deoxygenated blood mixes with oxygenated blood, often due to a 'hole in the heart' (septal defect).

qe: Which wave in the ECG is usually used to calculate the 'Heart Rate'?
e: The distance between two consecutive R-waves (R-R interval) is the standard for measuring heart rate.

qe: Which type of blood vessel is 'Fenestrated' to allow for high filtration (e.g., in kidneys)?
e: Fenestrated capillaries have small pores (fenestrae) that increase their permeability.

qe: What is 'Orthostatic Hypotension'?
o: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
e: Gravity pulls blood to the legs, and the heart must quickly adjust to maintain flow to the brain.

qe: The 'Windkessel Effect' is a term associated with the elasticity of the:
e: Elastic arteries expand and recoil, smoothing out the pressure changes from the heart's pumping.

qe: Which 'Blood Group' is known as the 'Bombay Blood Group' (Hh phenotype)?
o: A very rare group lacking the H-antigen
e: Discovered in Mumbai, people with this group can only receive blood from other Bombay Blood Group donors.

qe: What is 'Erythropoietin' (EPO)?
o: A hormone that stimulates RBC production
e: EPO is produced mainly by the kidneys in response to low oxygen levels in the blood.

qe: The 'T-wave' represents which electrical event?
e: It represents the recovery phase of the ventricles as they prepare for the next contraction.

qe: Which of the following prevents 'Blood Clotting' inside our healthy blood vessels?
e: Heparin is a natural anticoagulant produced by basophils and mast cells.

qe: What is 'Lymphedema'?
o: Swelling caused by blockage in the lymphatic system
e: It often occurs after surgery or infection where lymph nodes are damaged or removed.

qe: Which of the following acts as the 'Primary reservoir' for blood volume (60-70% of total blood)?
e: Veins are highly distensible and act as blood reservoirs, also called 'capacitance vessels'.

qe: The 'Left Coronary Artery' is often nicknamed the 'Widow-maker' because a blockage here affects the:
e: It supplies the majority of the blood to the left ventricle, the heart's main pump.

qe: In which animal does 'Single Circulation' occur?
e: In fish, blood passes through the heart only once during a complete circuit of the body.

qe: What is 'P-wave' in ECG indicative of?
e: It represents the electrical impulse starting from the SA node and spreading through the atria.

qe: The 'Circulatory System' was first accurately described by which scientist?
e: In 1628, William Harvey published his findings proving that blood circulates in a closed circuit pumped by the heart.

qe: What is the 'Frank-Starling Law' of the heart primarily concerned with?
e: It states that the force of ventricular contraction is proportional to the initial length of the muscle fibers (preload).

qe: Which of the following is the 'Universal Receiver' of plasma (not RBCs)?
e: While AB+ is the universal receiver for RBCs, O- is the universal receiver for plasma because its plasma lacks A and B antibodies.

qe: The 'Bohr Effect' describes the shift in the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve caused by:
e: An increase in CO2 or a decrease in pH (acidity) causes hemoglobin to release oxygen more readily to tissues.

qe: Which structure in the fetal heart allows blood to flow from the 'Right Atrium' directly to the 'Left Atrium'?
e: The Foramen Ovale allows blood to bypass the non-functional fetal lungs. It closes at birth to become the Fossa Ovalis.

qe: The 'Haldane Effect' refers to the property of Hemoglobin where:
o: Deoxygenation of blood increases its ability to carry CO2
e: When hemoglobin releases oxygen, it becomes a better carrier for carbon dioxide, helping in CO2 transport from tissues.

qe: Which chemical is the primary 'Vasodilator' released by the endothelium to lower blood pressure?
e: Nitric oxide relaxes the smooth muscles of the blood vessels, increasing the lumen diameter.

qe: What is 'Pulse Pressure'?
o: The average of Systolic and Diastolic
The difference between Systolic and Diastolic pressure
The maximum pressure in the aorta
e: For a BP of 120//80, the pulse pressure is 40 mmHg (120 minus 80).

qe: Which type of 'Shock' is caused by a massive loss of blood or fluids?
e: Hypovolemic shock occurs when there isn't enough blood for the heart to pump to the organs.

qe: The 'S-A Node' is located in the wall of which heart chamber?
e: It is situated in the upper wall of the right atrium, near the opening of the superior vena cava.

qe: Which of the following is a 'Negative Inotropic' agent (decreases heart contractility)?
e: Acetylcholine slows down the heart and reduces the force of contraction via the vagus nerve.

qe: What is the function of 'Carbonic Anhydrase' in the blood?
o: Speeding up the reaction between CO2 and water
e: Found mostly in RBCs, this enzyme is vital for transporting CO2 as bicarbonate ions.

qe: The 'Ejection Fraction' (EF) is a measurement of:
o: Percentage of blood leaving the heart each time it contracts
e: A normal EF is 55-70%. Lower values often indicate heart failure.

qe: Which 'Clotting Factor' is also known as the 'Christmas Factor'?
e: Deficiency of Factor IX causes Hemophilia B, also known as Christmas disease.

qe: What is 'Mean Arterial Pressure' (MAP)?
e: MAP is the average pressure in a patient's arteries during one cardiac cycle; it is a better indicator of organ perfusion.

qe: Which vessel is used as the 'Golden Standard' for measuring venous pressure (CVP)?
e: Central Venous Pressure (CVP) measures the pressure in the thoracic vena cava, near the right atrium.

qe: In an 'Isovolumetric Contraction', which valves are closed?
e: This is a brief moment where the ventricles contract but blood hasn't moved yet because all valves are shut.

qe: What is the 'Cardiac Reserve'?
o: The difference between resting and maximum cardiac output
The extra blood in the liver
The speed of the heart during sleep
e: Athletes have a very high cardiac reserve, allowing them to increase output significantly during exercise.

qe: The 'Pecquet's Cistern' (Cisterna Chyli) drains lymph primarily from which part of the body?
e: It is the origin of the thoracic duct, collecting fatty lymph (chyle) from the intestines.

qe: Which 'Leukocyte' is responsible for the 'Graft vs Host' reaction in transplants?
e: T-cells recognize foreign cells and initiate the immune attack that leads to transplant rejection.

qe: Which type of 'Hemophilia' is known as the 'Royal Disease' and is caused by a deficiency of Factor VIII?
e: Hemophilia A is the most common form and is an X-linked recessive genetic disorder.

qe: What is the 'R-R Interval' in an ECG used to measure?
e: The time between two consecutive R-waves tells the doctor the duration of one full cardiac cycle.

qe: The 'Hereditary' transmission of Blood Groups follows which genetic principle?
e: ABO blood groups show co-dominance (A and B are both expressed) and are governed by three alleles: I^A, I^B, and i.

qe: Which structure in the fetus becomes the 'Ligamentum Arteriosum' after birth?
e: The Ductus Arteriosus closes within days of birth, leaving behind a fibrous ligament.

qe: A 'ST-segment Elevation' on an ECG is a classic clinical sign of:
e: ST-elevation (STEMI) indicates that heart muscle is currently being damaged due to total artery blockage.

qe: Which 'Blood Group' contains no antibodies in its plasma?
e: Since AB+ has A, B, and Rh antigens, it does not produce antibodies against any of them.

qe: What is the function of 'Plasmin' in the blood?
e: Plasmin is an enzyme that breaks down fibrin mesh, preventing clots from growing too large.

qe: The 'Cardiac Index' (CI) relates the Cardiac Output to a person's:
e: CI = Cardiac Output // BSA. It helps doctors compare heart performance across different body sizes.

qe: Which condition is characterized by 'Microcytic Hypochromic' RBCs?
e: In iron deficiency, RBCs are smaller (microcytic) and paler (hypochromic) because they lack hemoglobin.

qe: The 'Hiss' sound or 'Murmur' heard through a stethoscope indicates:
o: Defective heart valves causing turbulent flow
e: Heart murmurs are often caused by 'leaky' valves (regurgitation) or 'narrow' valves (stenosis).

qe: Which 'Immunoglobulin' (Antibody) is small enough to cross the placenta from mother to fetus?
e: IgG provides the newborn with passive immunity during the first few months of life.

qe: What is the 'PR Interval' and why is it checked?
o: Time for impulse to travel from SA Node to Ventricles
e: A prolonged PR interval indicates a first-degree AV block (conduction delay).

qe: The 'Christmas Disease' is the other name for which disorder?
e: Named after Stephen Christmas, the first patient identified with Factor IX deficiency.

qe: Which chemical is the natural 'Antidote' to Heparin used in hospitals?
e: While Vitamin K reverses Warfarin, Protamine Sulfate is used to neutralize Heparin.

qe: In 'Sickle Cell Anemia', which amino acid is replaced by Valine in the hemoglobin chain?
e: This single point mutation causes RBCs to distort into a sickle shape under low oxygen.

qe: What is 'Stroke Volume' (SV) in terms of mathematical formula?
e: End-Diastolic Volume (full heart) minus End-Systolic Volume (remaining blood) equals Stroke Volume.

qe: Which heart chamber receives blood from the 'Coronary Sinus'?
e: The coronary sinus collects deoxygenated blood from the heart wall and dumps it into the right atrium.

qe: What is the 'Intrinsic Factor's' primary role in hematology?
e: Produced by the stomach, it is essential for the ileum to absorb B12 for RBC maturation.

qe: The 'Purkinje Fibers' conduct electrical impulses at which relative speed?
e: Fast conduction ensures the ventricles contract as a single unit to maximize pumping force.

qe: Which condition is characterized by 'Target Cells' in a blood smear?
e: Thalassemia is a genetic disorder affecting hemoglobin synthesis, showing characteristic target-shaped cells.

qe: What is the 'Apex' of the heart?
o: The pointed bottom part (Left Ventricle tip)
e: The apex points downward and to the left, where the heartbeat is most easily felt (Apical pulse).

qe: Which type of blood vessel contains 'Valves' to prevent backflow against gravity?
e: Veins have valves that work with skeletal muscles to push blood back up to the heart.

qe: The 'H-antigen' is the precursor for which blood groups?
e: Every person (except Bombay group) has H-antigen, which is converted to A or B antigens.

qe: What is 'Afterload'?
o: The resistance the heart must pump against (Blood Pressure)
e: Higher blood pressure increases the 'afterload', forcing the heart to work harder to open the valves.

qe: Which hormone is the primary regulator of 'Erythropoiesis' (RBC production)?
e: EPO is produced by the kidneys when they detect low oxygen levels (Hypoxia).

qe: The 'Q-wave' in an ECG specifically represents:
e: The Q-wave shows the electrical signal passing through the interventricular septum.

qe: Which 'Leukocyte' is the largest in size in a blood smear?
e: Monocytes are the largest WBCs and eventually migrate into tissues to become Macrophages.

qe: The 'Hepatic Portal Vein' is unique because it starts and ends in:
e: It begins in the intestinal capillaries and ends in the liver capillaries (sinusoids).

qe: What is 'Cardiac Output' for a heart rate of 70 and stroke volume of 70 ml?
e: Cardiac Output = HR x SV. 70 x 70 = 4900 ml//min.

qe: The 'Circulatory System' is a closed loop. Who proved this in 1628?
e: William Harvey's 'De Motu Cordis' correctly described the heart as a pump and blood as a circulating fluid.

qe: Which vitamin is most crucial for 'Blood Clotting'?
e: Vitamin K is needed by the liver to synthesize four major clotting factors.

qe: A 'Thrombus' that breaks loose and travels in the blood is called an:
e: An embolus can eventually get stuck and block blood flow to a vital organ (Embolism).

qe: What is the function of 'Albumins' in the plasma?
e: Albumin keeps water inside the blood vessels; low albumin leads to swelling (Edema).

qe: The 'Spleen' is considered the graveyard for:
e: Old and damaged Red Blood Cells are trapped and broken down in the spleen.

qe: Which part of the heart is known as the 'Pace-setter'?
e: The Atrio-ventricular (AV) node receives and delays the signal from the SA node.

qe: In which blood vessel is the 'Velocity' of blood the lowest?
e: Blood moves slowest in capillaries to allow maximum time for nutrient and gas exchange.

qe: Which organ receives oxygenated blood from the 'Hepatic Artery'?
e: The liver is unique; it gets oxygen from an artery but most of its blood volume from a vein (Portal vein).

qe: Which type of WBC is primarily involved in 'Allergic Reactions'?
e: Eosinophil counts rise during allergic responses and parasitic infections.

qe: What is the 'Cardiac Cycle' duration at 75 beats per minute?
e: 60 seconds // 75 bpm = 0.8 seconds per cycle.

qe: The 'Bundle of His' divides into right and left branches within the:
e: The branches run down the septum toward the apex of the heart.

qe: Which chamber of the heart pumps blood to the 'Lungs'?
e: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary artery.

qe: The 'Lubb' sound (S1) is caused by the closure of:
e: It marks the start of ventricular systole.

qe: What is 'Hemolysis'?
e: Hemolysis releases hemoglobin into the plasma, often due to mismatched blood or toxins.

qe: Which element is essential for the function of 'Hemoglobin'?
e: Iron in the ferrous state binds the oxygen molecule.

qe: The 'SA Node' is known as the heart's pacemaker because it:
o: Has the fastest rate of spontaneous depolarization
e: It fires 70-80 times per minute, overriding all other potential pacemakers.

qe: What is 'Atherosclerosis'?
e: Plaques made of fat and cholesterol narrow the arteries and can cause heart attacks.

qe: Which blood vessel has 'Thin Walls' and valves?
e: Veins operate under low pressure and need valves to keep blood moving toward the heart.

qe: The 'Universal Donor' group O- can donate to O+ because:
o: O- lacks A, B, and Rh antigens
e: Group O- blood is 'naked' and won't be rejected by any other group.

qe: What is the primary function of 'WBCs'?
e: Leukocytes identify and destroy pathogens like bacteria and viruses.

qe: What is 'Infarction'?
o: Tissue death due to inadequate blood supply
e: Myocardial infarction is the medical name for a heart attack caused by dead heart tissue.

qe: The first 'Heart Transplant' was performed by:
e: Dr. Christian Barnard performed the world's first human-to-human heart transplant in 1967.

qe: What is the significance of the 'QRS Complex' in an ECG?
e: The QRS complex represents the large electrical impulse triggering the ventricles to pump.

qe: The 'Lacteal' in the intestinal villi helps in the absorption of:
e: Lacteals are specialized lymph vessels that transport absorbed fats into the lymphatic system.

qe: What is 'CAD' in the context of the circulatory system?
e: CAD is the narrowing of the arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle.

qe: In an 'AB positive' person, which antibodies are present in the plasma?
e: Since they have A, B, and Rh antigens, they cannot have antibodies against them without attacking their own blood.

qe: Which pigment is responsible for the red color of human blood?
e: Hemoglobin is an iron-containing protein in red blood cells that binds with oxygen.
